decisions.reason: As a niche citrus-specific crate with only limited website prominence, it carries relatively low visible commitment, so disappointing traction would be easier for management to abandon despite the initial launch effort.

This foldable large container had the strongest sustained public presentation and fits the firm's core reusable-logistics strategy, so sunk costs and prior commitment make management likely to persist.
Although it was only mentioned rather than heavily promoted, a stackable plastic crate is close to the firm's established product base, which supports continuing it as an incremental portfolio item.

The medium-duty rackable pallet appears to be a modest line extension with limited public commitment, but its clear fit with the firm's pallet business still makes continued support somewhat more likely than withdrawal.
The spill-retention pallet had an initial dedicated page, indicating some investment and public commitment, so management is likely to keep it a bit longer even if it has become less prominent.
This pallet variant received visible launch support and remains closely aligned with the firm's core reusable transport-packaging capabilities, which encourages continued commitment.
